summary_md: **Ai2 ([@allen_ai](https://x.com/allen_ai/status/2115120549680521403))** (Ai2) releases an eval of LLM novelty judges for research ideas. The thread explains the benchmark mines ICLR 2026 reviews for originality comments; on human-vs-AI idea pairs GPT-5.4 picked the human idea 93.5% of the time when asked which reviewers judged novel but only 40.9% when asked which was novel; prompt changes helped some judges and hurt others; and two purpose-built novelty judges underperformed a prompted Claude Opus 4.6 baseline. Data, paper, code and blog are linked.

referenced_urls.title: Old Ideas, Novel Problems: The Instability of LLM-Based Novelty Evaluation
Can we trust LLMs to judge whether a research idea is novel? | Ai2

relevance: Cautions against trusting LLM novelty judgments in automated research loops.

media.description: Illustration of a lightbulb (an idea) radiating to six neural-network icons, each marked with a green check or a dark X, depicting LLM judges disagreeing about whether an idea is novel.

Slide 'Building the test from ICLR 2026 peer reviews': originality comments split into 154 papers with only praise (top 10% in area, stronger evidence of novelty) and 145 with only criticism (bottom 10%, weaker evidence).
media.ocr_text:
Building the test from ICLR 2026 peer reviews
"…a completely new, critical, and timely research problem" Only praise, Rated top 10% in its area → 154 papers with stronger evidence of novelty
"…the theoretical contribution is not highly novel…" Only criticism, Rated bottom 10% in its area → 145 papers with weaker evidence of novelty

media.description: Bar chart 'How AI models judged novelty in pairs of human- and AI-written research ideas': share of 154 pairs where each model picked the reviewer-praised idea under two prompts, from Claude Opus 4.6 (100.0% / 72.7%) down to Claude Sonnet 4.5 (60.4% / 36.4%).
media.ocr_text:
How AI models judged novelty in pairs of human- and AI-written research ideas
Which idea did reviewers judge to be novel? / Which idea is novel?
Claude Opus 4.6 100.0% / 72.7%
GPT-5.2 81.8% / 76.0%
Claude Opus 4.5 92.2% / 58.4%
GPT-5.1 79.2% / 56.5%
GPT-5.4 93.5% / 40.9%
Claude Sonnet 4.5 60.4% / 36.4%
154 pairs, each with a human-written idea praised as novel by ICLR reviewers and one generated by Claude Sonnet 4.5.

media.description: Bar chart 'How well Claude Opus 4.6 judged novelty': a simple prompt with no paper search scores 85, versus baselines AI-Scientist 77 and Idea Novelty Checker 64.
media.ocr_text:
How well Claude Opus 4.6 judged novelty
Simple prompt (no paper search; low reasoning, majority vote across 3 calls): 85
AI-Scientist (compares each idea with papers it finds): 77
Idea Novelty Checker (compares each idea with 10 related papers): 64
Score of 100 = every reviewer-praised idea judged novel and every AI-written idea judged not novel
